title: A spray that hits both sides
hook: A spray kills pests and their predators at the same rate. What happens to the pests?

doesNotKnow: the Lotka-Volterra model and its cycles

misconception: Killing a pest and its predator at the same rate must leave the pest the same or lower.
objective: The learner can explain that in the simple predator-prey model the average prey level is the level at which predators break even, so extra deaths for both species raise the average prey and lower the average predators.

claims.text: In the Lotka-Volterra model dx/dt = ax - bxy, dy/dt = cxy - dy, populations cycle and the long-run average prey is d/c and the average predator a/b; an extra death rate e on both makes them (d + e)/c and (a - e)/b.
claims.source: Integrate d(ln y)/dt = cx - d - e over one cycle: the left side is 0, so the time average of x is (d + e)/c; likewise for y. Murray, J. D., Mathematical Biology I (Springer), ch. 3.

claims.text: On the stage (a = b = c = d = 1, thousands, months), spray strength 20% raises the average pests from about 1,000 to 1,200 and lowers average predators from about 1,000 to 800; the reveal quotes the numbers for the strength the learner set.
claims.source: Demo.tsx run(): RK4, dt = 0.01, 600 months from (1.5, 1): averages 1.000/1.000 at e = 0, 1.199/0.800 at e = 0.2, 1.398/0.600 at e = 0.4 (checked with node).

claims.text: In this model pests breed on their own, while predators can only grow by eating pests; the average pest number is where predators exactly break even, so faster predator deaths raise it.
claims.source: Predator break-even: cxy = (d + e)y gives x = (d + e)/c; follows from c1.

claims.text: Volterra built this model in 1926 to explain why predatory fish made up more of the Adriatic catch when fishing paused in World War I.
claims.source: Volterra, V. (1926), 'Fluctuations in the abundance of a species considered mathematically', Nature 118: 558-560 (data from U. D'Ancona on Fiume/Trieste fish markets). Withdrawn from the learner-facing text in v2 (aside removed from the reveal); the sentence is no longer shown.

claims.text: The stage is a toy model: spray strength is an extra per-capita death rate per month added equally to both species; real farms and ecosystems are messier.
claims.source: Modelling choice in Demo.tsx; strength 20% means e = 0.2 per month.

recall.question: In a simple predator-prey model, a disease makes both prey and predators die a little faster. What happens to the long-run average number of prey?
recall.why: Average prey sits where predators break even. Predators that die faster need more prey to break even, so the prey average rises (and the predator average falls).
